title: October Roads in Korea Turn Red

slides.headline: In October, Korean roads **turn red.**
slides.note: Chili peppers, laid out to dry in the sun.

slides.headline: It's **chili pepper** season
slides.body: From late summer into autumn, farmers spread fresh red peppers anywhere flat and sunny: yards, rooftops, even road shoulders.

slides.headline: They become **gochugaru**
slides.body: Dried and ground, the peppers turn into gochugaru (고춧가루), the red flakes behind kimchi, stews and most red dishes.

slides.headline: Timed for **kimjang**
slides.body: In November comes kimjang (김장), when families make a winter's worth of kimchi. That takes a lot of chili flakes, made now.

slides.headline: Why not **a machine?**
slides.body: Dryers are faster. But sun-dried peppers, called taeyangcho (태양초), sell for more. Many say they taste sweeter and look brighter.

slides.headline: Asphalt is **flat and hot**
slides.body: A country road gets full sun all day. Drying crops on it is illegal and risky, yet every autumn some farmers still do.

slides.headline: Spices in a jar. **Or spices on the road.**
slides.body: In many countries chili flakes just appear on a shelf. In Korea you can still drive past them drying.

slides.headline: Days in the sun **for one batch**
slides.body: Up to two weeks, flipped by hand every day. A machine dryer takes about two days.

slides.headline: Red roads mean **kimchi is coming.**
slides.body: Those red rows by the road are the first step of a Korean winter table.

slides.headline: Korea, explained **by a Korean.**
slides.body: Follow for the context behind the things Korea does.
slides.graphic: Korean countryside village at dusk with a persimmon tree, softly blurred behind the text.

caption:
Every autumn, roads and rooftops in rural Korea turn red with chili peppers drying in the sun.

They become gochugaru, the flakes behind kimchi, and sun-dried ones still sell for more than machine-dried.

What gets laid out to dry where you live?
reply: One more: buyers test sun-dried peppers by holding them up to the light. Good taeyangcho is glossy and almost see-through, and the seeds rattle when you shake it. Machine-dried ones look darker and duller. Markets still sell them by the geun, about 600g. What does your family still insist on buying the old-fashioned way?
fact_check: 5장: 태양초가 건조기 고추(화건초)보다 비싸게 거래 — 농산물 시세 보도 다수. 맛 평가는 '많은 사람이 말한다'로 처리.
6장: 도로에 농산물 말리기는 도로법상 적치 금지·교통사고 위험으로 경찰·지자체가 매년 단속·계도 — 확인 필요.
8장: 태양초 천일건조 10~15일, 건조기 약 2일(48시간 안팎) — 농촌진흥청·농업 매체 설명 기준, 수치는 지역·날씨에 따라 다름.
댓글: 고추 1근=600g, 태양초 감별(빛 투과·씨 소리) — 일반적 설명.
